title: Sparkline pin preview carousel: compact version chooser with performance preview
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and deliver a compact ‘version chooser’ widget for the Console model card that surfaces recent performance profiles inline. The widget is a horizontally scrollable carousel of available versions; each card shows name, pinned badge (if applicable), a 7-day sparkline for median latency, token cost estimate, and a quick-pin button that opens a lightweight rollout sheet. The goal is to reduce time-to-pin from the current multi-step flow and provide immediate perf context for customers making version decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Compact carousel appears on model detail header and respects tenant feature flags
Each version card shows version id, semantic label (stable/canary), 7-day median latency sparkline, avg token cost, and last-published timestamp
Quick-pin launches a rollout sheet pre-filled with previous pin settings and allows setting percentage and staged windows (canary->ramp->full)
Compare modal compares up to 3 selected versions with side-by-side perf metrics and example responses
Performance profiles used for sparklines are read-only snapshots; publishing a new profile from the sheet triggers the existing publish flow
Widget meets baseline accessibility: keyboard focus order, ARIA labels, and 4.5:1 contrast for primary text
Telemetry events emitted: open_carousel, preview_card_click, quick_pin_initiated, publish_profile_clicked

Eng: Feasibility review for sparkline data path and caching (Liam)
Eng: Implement carousel component, rollout sheet, and compare modal (Frontend)

decisions: Show 7-day median latency instead of mean to reduce noise from outliers
Limit carousel preview to top 12 recent versions to keep rendering cheap
Quick-pin uses optimistic UI: local UI shows staged pin while backend confirms and falls back if constraint violation occurs
